description: September theme: Applied Public Health PROTECT (Prevention and Response for Outbreaks, Threats, and Emergencies through Capacitation and Training) is a CDC-funded UCSF-led global health security project implemented from 2021–2026, focused on strengthening countries’ capacity to detect, assess, and respond to public health threats through stronger surveillance systems, digital tools, and public health intelligence. In the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), PROTECT works closely with Ministries of Health and regional partners to advance event-based surveillance, health information systems, and data-driven decision-making. This Global Spotlight will explore the MENA experience through perspectives from health informatics program leaders, regional software developers, and Ministry of Health representatives from Egypt and Jordan, with a focus on how locally adapted digital innovations and stronger surveillance systems can improve early warning, information sharing, and public health preparedness. Speakers Ahmed Abouzaid, BS in Computer Engineering, is a Senior Software Engineer at UCSF. He builds and strengthens health information systems that support public health programs and enable data-driven decision-making.Mohammed Abu Meshref, with a degree in Information Technology, is a Software Developer based in Amman, Jordan. He focuses on building health related solutions and is passionate about productivity, helping others, and creating digital products that make a difference.Farah Massoud, MPH is a MENA Program Manager at UCSF IGHS where she leads regional initiatives to strengthen disease surveillance, epidemic intelligence, and public health emergency preparedness across the Middle East and North Africa. Her work focuses on cross-border disease surveillance, digital surveillance systems, event-based surveillance, and data-driven decision-making, in close collaboration with key national and international stakeholders, including Ministries of Health, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and regional public health partners.David Mugume, BSc in Health Information Systems (HIS), has extensive experience designing, implementing, and managing HIS solutions and teams in the public health sector. As Deputy Technical Director for Global Health Informatics, he supports the development of data and analytics systems, interoperability efforts, and Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems across multiple countries. With over eight years in public health and 14 years in software engineering, he has successfully led HIS initiatives in the Caribbean, sub-Saharan Africa, and the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. Mugume is also currently completing a Master’s degree in International Public Health at Liverpool John Moores University.Additional guest speakers to be announced. Facilitator: mike Reid, MD, MPH, MA is a faculty member at UCSF IGHS, where his work focuses on global health policy, sustainability, and the transition toward more country-led, integrated systems of care. He is also a practicing HIV clinician at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital. He co-leads the new Center for Applied Public Health (CAPH) at UCSF IGHS. From 2023 to 2026, Reid served as Chief Science Officer for the U.S. President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) in the Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy at the U.S. Department of State. In this role, he led PEPFAR’s scientific agenda and helped shape global health policy at the intersection of HIV, health systems, and emerging technologies. Earlier in his career, Reid led the secretariat for the Lancet Commission on Tuberculosis and directed multiple PEPFAR-supported programs in partnership with academic institutions across sub-Saharan Africa, focused on strengthening HIV service delivery and health system performance. He currently serves as Chair of the Lancet Global Health Commission on HIV and AI, where he is helping to define a forward-looking agenda at the intersection of technology, equity, and global health systems. He holds medical degrees from the University of Cambridge and Imperial College London, and an MPH from the University of California, Berkeley. Read related blog pieces by Farah Massoud: Strengthening Early Warning Systems: Rebuilding Egypt’s Event-Based Surveillance System, April 2026Strengthening Jordan’s Integrated Electronic Reporting System, June 2026Series Goals: The Global Partner Spotlight series through the UCSF Institute for Global Health Science (IGHS) Connect program highlights the work of partners around the world. The sessions provide a window into the priorities, challenges, and innovations of our collaborators in-country. For questions, please contact: IGHSConnect@ucsf.edu

description: Presented by Dr. John Brown from UCSF’s Threat Management Team, this training will provide leaders (supervisors, managers, directors, and above) with practical guidance and resources for responding when their team members are impacted by potential or actual incidents of workplace violence or threats of violence. Leaders will learn about applicable UCSF resources, protocols, and points of contact for managing a range of concerning situations involving their employees, including threats of violence, domestic violence concerns, stalking, and suicidal statements or other indications of potential self-harm. Emphasis will be placed on helping leaders understand their role, respond appropriately and safely, and engage the appropriate UCSF resources when situations require additional assessment, intervention, or support. Additional focus will be given to: • Recognizing common stress reactions in team members • Communicating effectively and compassionately in a crisis • Promoting a sense of safety and stability • Connecting employees with appropriate support Responding effectively in a moment of crisis can provide a team with increased safety, stability, and confidence. This allows for more resiliency in the aftermath of a critical incident supporting recovery and team cohesion. BIO: Dr. Brown serves as UCSF’s Threat Management Team Lead, in addition to his role as a licensed Clinical Psychologist with the Faculty and Staff Assistance Program and his private practice. He earned his master’s and doctoral degrees in Clinical Psychology from The Wright Institute in Berkeley, following a bachelor’s degree in History from Portland State University. Throughout his career, Dr. Brown has contributed to the field of psychological care in a variety of settings, including as a clinical psychologist with the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, where he specialized in caring for patients experiencing acute psychological distress. He joined UCSF’s Threat Management Team in 2016 and assumed the role of team lead in 2022. His combination of clinical expertise, academic training, and experience in threat management reflects his commitment to supporting the psychological well-being and safety of the UCSF community.

description: "Brain Zaps" and Other Withdrawal Symptoms Among People Using Alpha-2 Agonists in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania Meredith Meacham, PhD, MPH • Assistant Professor • Dept. of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences • UCSF Weill Institute for Neurosciences --------------------------------- The UCSF Drug Use Research Group (DURG) is a city-wide seminar attended by faculty, postdoctoral fellows, graduate students, and other Bay Area investigators centering on persons who use drugs. The DURG was founded in 2005 after a friendly debate between an epidemiologist and anthropologist on the merits of quantitative versus qualitative research methods. These monthly meetings provide a community platform for new and established investigators to present their works-in-progress, consult on new or related research and policy questions, and prepare for grant applications, conferences, and publications in a supportive environment. The seminar has been successful in cultivating new research collaborations, mentorship, and sustaining interdisciplinary and interprofessional dialogue between those engaged in basic sciences, epidemiology, clinical research, and qualitative methods. Our meetings are not recorded or live-streamed. If you would like to attend the seminar or present your work for dissemination, collaboration, and/or peer review, please contact Leslie Suen, MD, MAS: Leslie.Suen@ucsf.edu

description: Dear Residents and Fellows, Patient Care Fund Application – Due Friday, 9/25/26 In partnership with (and funded through!) UCSF Health and the Office of Graduate Medical Education (GME), we are pleased to announce this year's Patient Care Fund (PCF) call for applications! The PCF seeks proposals from and led by trainees that will improve the quality of patient care at UCSF. Applications are reviewed using the following criteria: Patient Care Impact: Only projects focused on improving tangible care for UCSF Health patients will be funded. Projects will be assessed for relative direct impact and relative long-term benefits to the patient population. Sustainability & Continuity: The proposal will be reviewed based on the potential for ongoing sustainable improvement for patients. If applicable, the proposal should demonstrate the source of ongoing funding necessary to sustain the project long term. Projects with sustained benefits to patients will be given a higher priority. Repeat proposals for projects that have been previously funded will not be considered. [Pilot, longevity] Budget Criteria: Funds are not intended to provide research, staffing, salary support, entertainment expenses, or other expenses inconsistent with UCSF Health or UCSF campus policies. Projects involving educational materials must also include a Patient Education Committee review and Interpreting and Translation Services if translations are needed (and highly suggested for more inclusive patient outreach). Examples of past funded proposals: Children’s books for pediatric clinic waiting areasPediatric hygiene kits to provide hair care items to patients with curly or coiled hairEducational pamphlets, magnets, and posters for pediatric or birthing patients"CARE" carts with medical resources, games, and art for geriatric inpatient unitsIndividualized patient gowns for breast cancer patients coming for multiple weekly radiation therapyArt supplies for a pediatrics art day event or art kits for geriatric / pediatric patientsLiveWell comics for pediatric patients with Irritable Bowel DiseaseTake-home culturally congruent cookbooks for discharge medicine patientsTake-home sunscreen / moisturizer kit for dermatology patientsProposals are due: Friday, September 26, 2025 Application Link: UCSF Patient Care Fund (2026-2027) For more information, see our PCF FAQ or visit our PCF Website. We are committed to improving the quality of patient care at UCSF and are happy to help you develop your idea, so please do not hesitate to reach out to us with any follow-up requests/ questions! Contact: Marisa McFarlane (marisa.mcfarlane@ucsf.edu)

description: Are you aged 18-early 40s, living with a brain tumor? Would you like to connect with other young adults living with a similar diagnosis? You are invited to join our monthly online peer-led UCSF Young Adult Brain Tumor Support Group (YABS). This is a safe and welcoming place for us to authentically express ourselves, build resilience, and encourage one another to live our best lives. We don’t shy away from the hard stuff, but we also make a lot of room for joy. We laugh, cry, get real, have fun, and share our lives—most importantly, we’re building community! Our group is facilitated by peers who know what it’s like to live with a brain cancer diagnosis as a young adult. This group is also open to non-UCSF patients. We meet on the last Thursday of each month, from 6:30 - 8:00 pm (PT). Registration link. Please Note: As part of the registration process, your enrollment and continued participation is subject to review by our clinical and administrative team. This helps us ensure that the group is appropriate for you and supports a positive and supportive experience for all members. You will be notified via email once the review is complete and your enrollment is confirmed. About the Facilitators: Dace has worked in a variety of industries as a young adult (hospitality, technology sales, event photography, etc). The one thing that has tied them all together is people. As a lifelong learner, he is committed to developing resilience by leaning in with curiosity and learning to embody a growth mindset no matter the circumstance. He enjoys surfing, music of every conceivable kind, and the quiet comfort of extended time with Mother Nature. Phoebe (they/them) is a former Californian living in Seattle, Washington. Diagnosed with a grade II oligodendroglioma in 2015, they find solace, inspiration, and joy in connecting deeply with other young adults living with brain tumors. They aspire to spend most of their time whipping up something involved and delicious in the kitchen or outside, hiking and camping with their pup, Snack. Sponsored by the UCSF Sheri Sobrato Brain Cancer Survivorship Program and the Anna Kathrene Smith Brain Tumor Research and Patient Care Fund.

description: Osher WISE Course: What Should I Take? Making Informed Choices About Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Wednesdays, October 7–28, 6:00-7:30 p.m. PT Approximately 1 in 5 adults uses a plant-based herbal supplement, and 1 in 2 uses a vitamin or mineral product. Many people do not tell their health care providers about the supplements they are taking. This communication gap can increase the risk of interactions with prescription medications, existing health conditions, and other treatments. As the use of dietary supplements continues to grow, it is important for people to understand how to evaluate these products, recognize their potential benefits and risks, and identify which supplements are supported by strong scientific evidence. Accessing reliable, evidence-based information can help everyone make safer, more informed decisions about their health. This four-week course will help participants learn essential tips for dietary supplement selection and evidence-based information on the effectiveness and potential risks for supplements and herbals commonly used for longevity, heart health, bone health, and other uses. This course is chaired by UCSF Clinical Pharmacy Faculty, Dr. Candy Tsourounis and Dr. Cathi Dennehy. October 7: Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Essentials: What You Need to Know October 14: Supplements for Healthy Aging: What's Popular, and Should I Take It? October 21: Longevity: Can Supplements Help You Live Longer and Healthier? October 28: Vitamins and Minerals: What Makes Sense for You Register here Our educational programming, formerly known as Osher Mini Medical School for the Public, has been reimagined as Osher WISE (Well-being and Integrative Science for Everyone). This public education program offers courses on integrative health topics that are current and compelling, providing an opportunity for community members to become active, informed participants in their own journey to health and well-being. https://osher.ucsf.edu/Osher-WISE, powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform
